comparisons.peer_summary: Corporate/Other revenues decreased to $668 million from $2.1 billion, largely driven by net investment securities losses from portfolio repositioning and higher funding costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citigroup disclose that investment securities losses in 2024 were driven by the repositioning of their respective investment securities portfolios. JPM reports that these losses decreased compared to the prior year, specifically citing lower losses on sales of U.S. Treasuries and MBS associated with this repositioning in Treasury and CIO. Citigroup similarly attributes its net investment securities losses (which contributed to a decline in Corporate/Other revenues) to the repositioning of the investment securities portfolio, though JPM provides more specific detail on the magnitude trend (decreased) and asset types (Treasuries/MBS) involved in the repositioning activity.

sentences.text: Investment securities losses decreased, reflecting lower losses on sales of securities, primarily U.S. Treasuries and U.S. GSE and government agency MBS, associated with repositioning the investment securities portfolio in Treasury and CIO.

Corporate/Other revenues decreased to $668 million, compared to $2.1 billion in the prior year, largely driven by the net investment securities losses due to the repositioning of the investment securities portfolio and higher funding costs.

comparisons.peer_summary: All Other (managed basis) revenues decreased 20%, primarily due to lower revenues in Corporate/Other (driven by net investment securities losses from portfolio repositioning and higher funding costs) and Legacy Franchises (down 6% due to declines in Asia Consumer and Legacy Holdings Assets, partially offset by Mexico Consumer/SBMM).
comparisons.comparison: Citigroup's disclosure confirms that the decline in Corporate/Other revenues was largely driven by net investment securities losses due to portfolio repositioning, mirroring JPM's topic of investment securities losses associated with repositioning. While JPM explicitly states the losses decreased in 2024 compared to 2023, Citigroup's disclosure focuses on the contribution of these repositioning losses to a revenue decline without specifying if the absolute loss amount was higher or lower than the prior year, but the causal driver (repositioning) is identical.
